articles.title: CX Thunderstorm
articles.summary: Near-black charcoal with faint electric-blue and white lightning streaks, semi-matte and moody. Reads as near-black with a faint cold blue glimmer, like a storm night sky; the veins nearly vanish and only a few star points show.
articles.what: Dark charcoal gray → electric blue → white flash. Storm front rolling in. Up close: Very dark navy-black with thin branching pale-blue lightning veins, 1-2 px, forming a loose web of forks 20-80 px long with brighter star-like nodes where branches meet. Faint vertical rain streaks run through the whole surface. The veins are dim except at the nodes. From a distance: Reads as near-black with a faint cold blue glimmer, like a storm night sky; the veins nearly vanish and only a few star points show. Measured spec (average): metal 172, roughness 158, coat 150. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put CX Thunderstorm on the hood".
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: fine veins work on any panel
Hood and roof show the glints best
White, bright blue or yellow numbers read; dark numbers disappear.
None or one bold bright graphic: the dark, quiet ground lets it pop
Pairs well with: white, chrome, electric blue.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not bright blue lightning bolts: veins are faint and thin
Not a cloudy gradient: no cloud shapes, only fine veins and rain streaks
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, dark numbers.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 172 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 158 (semi-matte), clearcoat 150 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, dark numbers.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none or one bold bright graphic: the dark, quiet ground lets it pop; white or electric blue pinstripe: supports the storm colours
Patterns to avoid: lightning, cracks or web patterns: duplicate the veins; dark patterns: they vanish
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: makes the sparkle crisper; fine silver flake: adds more sky glitter
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Daily Driver
articles.summary: Perfectly smooth high-gloss paint with no flake, grain or pattern; a plain mirror-like colour panel. Takes your colour and gives plain smooth gloss, like fresh factory paint, with no grain, flake or pattern; only very faint waviness in the reflection.
articles.what: Up close: On the neutral grey input the paint is a perfectly flat panel with nothing on it. The spec strips on the right are stretched to full contrast, so the soft blotchy variation shown is only a tiny wobble in real life (roughness std 3, clearcoat std 6); no metal at all. From a distance: Takes your colour and gives plain smooth gloss, like fresh factory paint, with no grain, flake or pattern; only very faint waviness in the reflection. Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Daily Driver" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: plain gloss works everywhere
Hood and doors: show reflections best
Numbers read cleanly in any contrasting colour; the base is perfectly even.

Not a pearl or candy: there is no colour depth, it is plain colour with gloss
